items.title: Antonelli turns P19 into a home victory
items.summary: Antonelli recovered from his power-unit grid penalty to beat Russell, with Verstappen third. His decisive pass came on lap 50 after an earlier excursion through the gravel. Norris beat Piastri to fourth.
items.why_it_matters: The headline is the completed Mercedes one-two and Antonelli's recovery, not a pre-race prediction about damage limitation.

items.title: Red flag and VSC reshape the tyre comparison
items.summary: Russell stayed on the hards fitted during the early red flag. Antonelli took fresh mediums during the later VSC, while Verstappen switched to hards. That tyre-age split shaped the final fight for the win.
items.why_it_matters: Do not present this disrupted race as proof of an optimal green-flag pit window. Pit-lane elapsed times are also not stationary wheel-change times.

items.title: Separate the opening-lap dispute from Leclerc's later crash
items.summary: Hamilton's first-chicane battle with Leclerc cost him ground; Leclerc's separate lap-two crash at Curva Alboreto caused the red flag. In their Madrid follow-up, both drivers say they have cleared the air, with Leclerc accepting his Turn 2 error.
items.why_it_matters: Keep the incidents and dates distinct. The discussion afterward is not evidence of a new Ferrari team-orders policy.
